title: smart-routing fallback incident breadcrumbs - jordan
content:
Goal: quick breadcrumbs for what I tried during the EU regional failover incident (2026-02-27). Personal scratchpad - messy, rough.

Timeline (rough):
- 02:07 UTC: Alerts for increased p99 latency for eu-west-1 requests (customer-facing routing).
- 02:09 UTC: Smart-routing control-plane triggered regional fallback to us-central-1 for ~18% of EU traffic (policy: latency-first).
- 02:10 UTC: Customers report elevated error rates (502/504) and slower responses.
- 02:20 UTC: We temporarily pinned routing to eu variants and scaled eu pool (manual).
- 02:45 UTC: Errors subsided but some requests still hit fallback variant (quantized model) and produced degraded outputs.

Observed symptoms / logs (snippets):
- control-plane logs: \"[WARN] route-evaluator: no healthy endpoints for model-variant 'gptx-2b-q4_0' in eu-west-1, initiating fallback\"
- redis/kvs: intermittent timeouts (multi-get took 2500ms) around 02:08-02:12
- nginx-ingress: 502 bursts on node eu-ingress-3 (OOM kill??) but kube events show no OOMKilled pods
- model-serving logs (eu pool): \"healthcheck: instance heartbeat missed (last 18s)\" then \"reinitialized runtime\"

Commands I ran (notes inline):
- curl to control-plane route evaluator (internal API)
  curl -s -X POST \"https://control-plane.internal/route/evaluate\" -d '{\"region\":\"eu-west-1\",\"route\":\"customers/prod\"}' 
  -> response: {\"decision\":\"fallback\",\"target_region\":\"us-central-1\",\"reason\":\"no_healthy_variant\"}

- kubectl (checked pods, events):
  kubectl get pods -n serving -l pool=eu -o wide
  kubectl describe pod eu-model-1 -n serving  # looked for OOM/kubelet events - nothing obvious
  kubectl logs eu-model-1 -n serving --since=30m | grep -i health

- checked redis latency from control-plane hosts:
  redis-cli -h redis-eu-01 latency latest  # returned spikes ~2500 ms at 02:09

- verified KV cache sizes and eviction rates (prometheus query):
  sum(increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (instance)  -> small but present on redis-eu-02

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Transient healthcheck / heartbeat mismatch: instances briefly missed heartbeats (18s) causing route evaluator to mark variant unhealthy. Heartbeat TTL vs control-plane evaluation window mismatch.
   - Evidence: \"heartbeat missed (last 18s)\" in model logs; evaluator reason \"no_healthy_variant\".
   - Counter-evidence: pods show healthy after restart, but traffic already diverted.

2) Redis/KV latency causing model-serving to fail health probes (probe uses tiny kv read).
   - Evidence: redis latency spikes at same time window. Probe uses redis GET to validate caching layer.
   - Action: replicate redis read from a control-plane host (done) and we saw spikes.

3) Control-plane transient overload due to rollout job + high eval traffic -> slower decision path + false negatives.
   - Evidence: small spike in route-eval latency metrics around 02:06-02:11 (pending deeper look).

4) Ingress node flakiness causing upstream 502s unrelated to model variants (probably compounding noise).

Quick mitigation we did / timeline of interventions:
- 02:12: temporarily lowered route-evaluator sensitivity (increased min healthy threshold) to avoid immediate fallback for 60s windows.
- 02:20: manual pin of critical customers in eu routing table to eu-variants (hotfix).
- 02:22: scaled eu-serving pool by +2 instances (immediate capacity).
- 02:40: rolled back temporary sensitivity change once redis/eu nodes stabilized.

Follow-ups / action items (to turn into tickets):
- ACTION-A: Align heartbeat TTL and route-evaluator evaluation window (owner: eng-serving-runtime) - likely change: increase heartbeat grace to 30s or make evaluator tolerant to short gaps.
- ACTION-B: Add redis latency SLO alert that's specifically tied to health-probe failures (owner: infra).
- ACTION-C: Improve incidenct runbook for smart-routing fallback: clear steps for pinning routing, verifying model-variant health, and when to scale pools. (owner: SRE/Platform)
- ACTION-D: Postmortem draft (INC-2341) - collect more traces (route-eval traces, control-plane logs, redis instance CPU/latency graphs).

Quick checks to reproduce locally (dev env):
- Simulate redis latency by adding artificial delay in test harness and run route-eval to see if fallback triggers.
- Run the heartbeat-miss script (scripts/heartbeat-test) across a few model instances to test evaluator tolerance.

Notes / random thoughts:
- Could also consider decoupling health-probe dependency on redis for probe path (use local process-level health instead).
- If evaluator has a voting mechanism across instances, ensure margin for partial transient failures (eg require 2 consecutive missed checks before marking down).
- We should instrument the fallback decision with the exact cause chain: e.g., \"healthcheck->redis-latency->probe-fail->evaluator-decision\" so postmortem can reconstruct easily.

Unresolved questions to triage in follow-up meeting:
- Was there any concurrent deployment to eu that increased memory pressure? (check rollout events around 01:50-02:10)
- Is redis-eu-02 underprovisioned (CPU high)? Need heap/profile.
- Did any autoscaler activity coincide (horizontal pod autoscaler churning)?

Next quick steps tomorrow (my plan):
- Pull full control-plane trace for 02:00-02:30 and annotate (Jordan).
- Create ACTION tickets and assign owners (today).
- Run redis latency repro in staging (with infra).

TL;DR: Transient redis latency likely caused health probes to briefly fail -> route evaluator marked eu model-variant unhealthy -> regional fallback to us-central produced higher latency + some degraded outputs. Immediate fixes were pinning routes and scaling eu pool. Need heartbeat/evaluator alignment and better redis-probe instrumentation.

Scratch log / misc commands I left in my shell history:
- curl https://control-plane.internal/route/evaluate -d '{\"region\":\"eu-west-1\",\"route\":\"customers/prod\"}'
- kubectl -n serving get pods -l pool=eu -o wide
- redis-cli -h redis-eu-01 latency latest
- kubectl logs eu-model-1 -n serving --since=60m | grep -i heartbeat

End of scratchpad. Will formalize into postmortem if signal holds.
